change.title: pr-3-flat
change.description: feat(upsampling) - Support upsampled error count with performance optimizations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Substring match treats negated and OR'd error filters as error-only queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` (line 137) checks `"event.type:error" in query`, a substring test. It also matches `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` sends every discover query through this check (lines 122-124), so for an allowlisted project a discover query for non-error events gets `upsampled_count() as count` (organization_events_stats.py:295-296 and 298-299). The module itself says sample_weight does not exist for transactions (line 106), so those rows add nothing to the sum and the series reads 0 or too low, with no error. The unit test (tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py:77-88) only covers the exact `event.type:transaction` string, and the integration tests never send a negated or OR'd error query (grep of tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py). Suggested fix for this failure: only treat the query as error-focused when `event.type:error` is a standalone positive term, i.e. not preceded by `!` and not combined with OR, and add a test for `!event.type:error` and for the OR case.
findings.originReason: The whole helper module is new in this diff.

verification.reason: `_is_error_focused_query` uses a plain substring test, so `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both return True. For the discover dataset, `count()` then becomes `upsampled_count()` even though the query covers non-error events.

findings.title: toInt64 truncates the summed sample weights
findings.body: Does the stored sample_weight equal 1/client_sample_rate as a float, or int(1/rate) as event_manager.py:1564 computes for group times_seen? If it is fractional, `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` truncates a sum such as 9.9999… down to 9 whenever the sum lands just below an integer, which gives a silent undercount. If it is an integer per event, every event's weight is truncated (rate 0.3 gives 3, not 3.33). The only test uses rate 0.1, where 1/0.1 is exactly 10 and hides the problem. Which representation does Snuba use, and should the result be rounded rather than truncated?

verification.reason: Snuba computes and stores `sample_weight`, and that code is not in this repository. From here I cannot tell whether the column is a float or an integer, so I cannot say whether `toInt64(sum(...))` really undercounts.

findings.title: upsampled_count is not private, so every discover query can select it
findings.body: The new SnQLFunction has no `private=True`. Its siblings in this block do (`examples` at 1019, `rounded_timestamp` at 1027, `column_hash` at 1039). Private functions are rejected unless they appear in functions_acl (src/sentry/search/events/builder/base.py:737-738, fields.py:1515-1529). Without the flag, any discover request, including the public events-stats API, can use `upsampled_count()` in fields or yAxis, and it is not limited to error-upsampled projects. If the function is meant to be internal, mark it private like its siblings.

verification.reason: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction has no `private=True`, unlike `column_hash` next to it. The builder rejects only private functions that are missing from functions_acl, so any discover query can select `upsampled_count()`.

findings.title: Cache round-trip runs for every events-stats request before the dataset check
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` does `cache.get` (line 30) and, on a miss, `options.get` plus `cache.set` (lines 35-38) before `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` (lines 32 and 40). That check is pure and cheap, and it rejects every non-error dataset (transactions, metrics, spans, ...). So each events-stats call pays a cache round-trip even when the answer is already known to be False. `_get_event_stats` calls this on every invocation (organization_events_stats.py:220), and the dashboard split path calls `_get_event_stats` several times per request (lines 345-495). Evaluating the dataset and request check first would skip the cache for those datasets. The 60-second TTL also means an allowlist change takes up to a minute to take effect.

verification.reason: `cache.get` (and on a miss, `options.get` plus `cache.set`) runs before the cheap dataset/request check. Every events-stats call on a non-error dataset therefore pays for a cache round-trip even though the answer is always False.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller
findings.body: The repository has no caller of `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (grep: only the definition). Its docstring says it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes", but nothing in this PR or the allowlist code path calls it, so the 60-second TTL is the only invalidation. Either wire it into the allowlist change path or remove it and correct the docstring that claims it is required.

verification.reason: A grep of the repository finds only the definition of `invalidate_upsampling_cache` and no callers, even though its docstring says it should be called when the allowlist changes.

findings.title: Comments describe caching and optimization that the code does not do
findings.body: The comments at lines 218-226 call the check an "early upsampling eligibility check for performance optimization" whose "cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution", and say the separation "allows for better query optimization and caching". The check runs again in every `_get_event_stats` call, nothing is shared across calls beyond the 60-second cache entry, and no query is optimized. Lines 229-234, 274-277 and 294-296 apply the same transform in three places, with `final_columns` reassigned on the RPC path where it already holds the same value. The comments should describe what the code does, and the transform could be applied once.

verification.reason: The comments talk about an optimization and about shared caching that the code does not do: the check reruns on every `_get_event_stats` call, and the same transform is copied into three places. One detail in the claim is wrong, though. On the non-top RPC path (line 276), `final_columns` still holds the untransformed `query_columns`, so that reassignment is needed, not a no-op.

findings.title: Unrelated change to the topEvents error text
findings.body: The message changes from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1". This is not part of the upsampling change, it changes an API error string that clients may match, and no test asserts either string. Move it to a separate change, or revert it.

verification.reason: The error text changes and the change has nothing to do with upsampling. It is a grammar fix, and the new wording matches the sibling message in organization_events_timeseries.py:134, so the risk is low.

findings.title: Stray submodule pointer committed with the feature
findings.body: The diff adds `sentry-repo` as a gitlink (`Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`). Nothing in this change refers to it, and the head snapshot has no `.gitmodules` that declares it, so a clone cannot initialize it. It looks accidental. Remove it from this pull request. Confidence is medium because the snapshot may leave out `.gitmodules`.

verification.reason: The diff adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink. The head snapshot has no `.gitmodules` and nothing refers to the path, so the gitlink looks like an accidental commit.

findings.title: Test-only sample_rate shim diverges from ingestion and hides the allowlist gate
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` (lines 344-357) sets `sample_rate` for any project and accepts any float. Ingestion (`_derive_client_error_sampling_rate`, src/sentry/event_manager.py:774-787) sets it only for allowlisted projects, and only when 0 < rate <= 1. The integration tests patch only `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options` (tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py:3604-3607), so ingestion never sees the allowlist and never sets `sample_rate`. The shim is therefore the only thing that creates the weight the assertions rely on, and these tests exercise a path ingestion does not take for these projects. The broad `except Exception: pass` blocks (lines 351-357) would also hide a bad value. Either apply the same allowlist and range checks, or patch `sentry.event_manager.options` in the tests and let ingestion set the field.

verification.reason: Ingestion sets `sample_rate` only for allowlisted projects, and only when 0 < rate <= 1. The tests patch only `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options`, so ingestion never sees the allowlist and the factory shim is what supplies `sample_rate`. The shim has no allowlist or range check, and its broad `except` blocks would hide a bad value.

findings.title: Organization created with a direct model call instead of a test helper
findings.body: CLAUDE.md (Common Gotchas, item 7) says tests should use `self.create_*` helpers, not direct model creation. Line 20 calls `Organization.objects.create(name="test-org")`, and the test class is a `TestCase` that has `self.create_organization`. The organization is used only for `organization.id` in the cache-key path.

verification.reason: CLAUDE.md, Common Gotchas item 7, says tests should use `self.create_*` helpers. The new test calls `Organization.objects.create` directly instead.

findings.title: Test named 'with_transaction_events' does not test a mixed query
findings.body: `test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events` only queries `event.type:transaction`, so it checks that the transform is skipped for a transaction-only query. It does not cover the mixed or negated cases where the substring check in error_upsampling.py:137 misfires. No test in this file uses `!event.type:error` or an OR'd query with an allowlist. Rename the test, or add the negated and OR'd cases.

verification.reason: The test sends only `query: event.type:transaction`, so it covers a transaction-only query, not a mixed one. No test sends a negated or OR'd error query.

findings.title: Equations that use count() stay unweighted
findings.body: Only `final_columns` is transformed. `equations=self.get_equation_list(...)` at line 256 (and in the RPC top-N call at line 251) still reads the raw request, so an equation such as `count() * 2` shown next to the upsampled `count` series is computed from unweighted counts. The top-N ranking query (src/sentry/snuba/discover.py:491-505) is also left unweighted. Is it intended that equations and top-N selection use raw counts while the plain series uses weighted counts?

verification.reason: Only `final_columns` is transformed. Equations come straight from the request, and the top-N ranking query uses `selected_columns` and equations without weighting, so both stay on raw counts.

contracts.action: count() on an events-stats query is rewritten to upsampled_count() as count for allowlisted projects
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py:298-305 (same timeseries_query call with count() when no upsampling applies)
contracts.before_after: Immediately before scoped_dataset.timeseries_query, the column list changes from count() to upsampled_count() as count. The rest of the call is unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: Series values become sum(sample_weight). The response key stays 'count': get_function_alias returns the explicit alias (fields.py:685-686), and serialization uses query_columns (organization_events.py:563-568).
contracts.failure_mode: If sample_weight is not a readable column for the errors builder, the query fails. Failures from that would surface as an error response, not silently.
contracts.open_question: Does the events storage the errors builder queries expose sample_weight as a column? Nothing in this repository defines it (grep of src/ finds only the new code).

contracts.action: discover query with !event.type:error (or an OR'd error filter) on allowlisted projects
contracts.equivalent_path: The same query with count() and no transform (organization_events_stats.py:298-305)
contracts.before_after: count() is replaced with upsampled_count() as count, although the query is not error-focused.
contracts.visible_effect: Counts for non-error rows are computed as sum(sample_weight). The module comment says those rows have no sample_weight (error_upsampling.py:106), so the series reads 0 or too low.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong result. No error or log is produced.

contracts.action: First cache lookup for every events-stats call, through is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects
contracts.before_after: A new cache read happens before the dataset check and on every call to _get_event_stats. The cache is django.core.cache directly, with no try/except around it.
contracts.visible_effect: None on a hit. On a miss, one options read and one cache write.
contracts.failure_mode: If cache.get raises, the exception leaves _get_event_stats and fails every events-stats request, including non-error datasets and non-allowlisted orgs.
contracts.open_question: Does the configured cache backend raise or return None when Redis is unavailable?

contracts.action: New discover aggregate upsampled_count registered in DiscoverDatasetConfig
contracts.equivalent_path: Private siblings in the same block: examples (discover.py:1014-1020), rounded_timestamp (1021-1028), column_hash (1029-1040), all with private=True; access is gated by is_accessible at builder/base.py:737-738.
contracts.before_after: Nothing existing changes. The new name becomes callable in every discover query.
contracts.visible_effect: Public API accepts upsampled_count() in fields and yAxis.
contracts.failure_mode: No new failure. It is an exposure of an internal aggregate.

contracts.action: Test-only store_event shim sets sample_rate from contexts.error_sampling
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/event_manager.py:774-798 (_derive_client_error_sampling_rate), which is gated by the allowlist at line 776
contracts.before_after: Ingestion sets sample_rate only for allowlisted projects, in (0, 1]. The shim sets it for any project with a truthy value.
contracts.visible_effect: No effect on the product. Only tests that store events with error_sampling context are affected.
contracts.failure_mode: Test-only. Bad values are swallowed by the broad except blocks (factories.py:351-357).

contracts.equivalent_path: The same call's other arguments: selected_columns from get_field_list and equations from get_equation_list are unchanged. TopEventsQueryBuilder consumes timeseries_columns via categorize_columns (src/sentry/search/events/builder/discover.py:321-336).
contracts.before_after: Only the timeseries column changes, from count() to upsampled_count() as count. Equations and the top-N selection are not changed.
contracts.visible_effect: The series for the top events is weighted. Equations that use count() and the top-N ranking stay unweighted (finding on line 256).
contracts.failure_mode: No new failure path found. The ranking query in snuba/discover.py:491-505 is unchanged.

summary: No blockers. The main defect is in `_is_error_focused_query` (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:137): a substring match treats `!event.type:error` and OR'd error filters as error-only, so an allowlisted project's discover query for non-error rows gets `sum(sample_weight)` and silently wrong counts. The rest: `upsampled_count` lacks `private=True` (discover.py:1041), a `toInt64` truncation question (discover.py:1047), an unrelated topEvents message change (organization_events_stats.py:124), a stray `sentry-repo` gitlink, a test shim that diverges from ingestion (factories.py:344), a direct `Organization.objects.create` against CLAUDE.md, and a test whose name does not match its coverage. Open items: whether the events storage exposes `sample_weight` and how the cache backend fails on Redis errors. docs/adr/ does not exist in this snapshot, so no ADR check was possible. I did not read the full 3,700-line tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py; I read its header and the new class, and grepped the rest for the negated and OR'd error queries. I also read only the relevant parts of discover.py (around 990-1090) and factories.py (around 1000-1090). Nothing was built or run.
